NASB.1: 'My spirit is broken, my days are extinguished, The grave is [ready] for me.
NASB.2: 'Surely mockers are with me, And my eye gazes on their provocation.
NASB.3: 'Lay down, now, a pledge for me with Yourself; Who is there that will be my guarantor?
NASB.4: 'For You have kept their heart from understanding, Therefore You will not exalt [them].
NASB.5: 'He who informs against friends for a share [of the spoil], The eyes of his children also will languish.
NASB.6: 'But He has made me a byword of the people, And I am one at whom men spit.
NASB.7: 'My eye has also grown dim because of grief, And all my members are as a shadow.
NASB.8: 'The upright will be appalled at this, And the innocent will stir up himself against the godless.
NASB.9: 'Nevertheless the righteous will hold to his way, And he who has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.
NASB.10: 'But come again all of you now, For I do not find a wise man among you.
NASB.11: 'My days are past, my plans are torn apart, [Even] the wishes of my heart.
NASB.12: 'They make night into day, [saying], 'The light is near,' in the presence of darkness.
NASB.13: 'If I look for Sheol as my home, I make my bed in the darkness;
NASB.14: If I call to the pit, 'You are my father'; To the worm, 'my mother and my sister';
NASB.15: Where now is my hope? And who regards my hope?
NASB.16: 'Will it go down with me to Sheol? Shall we together go down into the dust?'

NKJV.1: “My spirit is broken, My days are extinguished, The grave is ready for me.
NKJV.2: Are not mockers with me? And does not my eye dwell on their provocation?
NKJV.3: “Now put down a pledge for me with Yourself. Who is he who will shake hands with me?
NKJV.4: For You have hidden their heart from understanding; Therefore You will not exalt them.
NKJV.5: He who speaks flattery to his friends, Even the eyes of his children will fail.
NKJV.6: “But He has made me a byword of the people, And I have become one in whose face men spit.
NKJV.7: My eye has also grown dim because of sorrow, And all my members are like shadows.
NKJV.8: Upright men are astonished at this, And the innocent stirs himself up against the hypocrite.
NKJV.9: Yet the righteous will hold to his way, And he who has clean hands will be stronger and stronger.
NKJV.10: “But please, come back again, all of you, For I shall not find one wise man among you.
NKJV.11: My days are past, My purposes are broken off, Even the thoughts of my heart.
NKJV.12: They change the night into day; ‘The light is near,’ they say, in the face of darkness.
NKJV.13: If I wait for the grave as my house, If I make my bed in the darkness,
NKJV.14: If I say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ And to the worm, ‘You are my mother and my sister,’
NKJV.15: Where then is my hope? As for my hope, who can see it?
NKJV.16: Will they go down to the gates of Sheol? Shall we have rest together in the dust?”

NLT.1:
“My spirit is crushed,
and my life is nearly snuffed out.
The grave is ready to receive me.
NLT.2:
I am surrounded by mockers.
I watch how bitterly they taunt me.
NLT.3:
“You must defend my innocence, O God,
since no one else will stand up for me.
NLT.4:
You have closed their minds to understanding,
but do not let them triumph.
NLT.5:
They betray their friends for their own advantage,
so let their children faint with hunger.
NLT.6:
“God has made a mockery of me among the people;
they spit in my face.
NLT.7:
My eyes are swollen with weeping,
and I am but a shadow of my former self.
NLT.8:
The virtuous are horrified when they see me.
The innocent rise up against the ungodly.
NLT.9:
The righteous keep moving forward,
and those with clean hands become stronger and stronger.
NLT.10:
“As for all of you, come back with a better argument,
though I still won’t find a wise man among you.
NLT.11:
My days are over.
My hopes have disappeared.
My heart’s desires are broken.
NLT.12:
These men say that night is day;
they claim that the darkness is light.
NLT.13:
What if I go to the grave
and make my bed in darkness?
NLT.14:
What if I call the grave my father,
and the maggot my mother or my sister?
NLT.15:
Where then is my hope?
Can anyone find it?
NLT.16:
No, my hope will go down with me to the grave.
We will rest together in the dust!”

AMP.1:
"My spirit is broken, my days are extinguished,
The grave is ready for me.
AMP.2:
"Surely there are mockers and mockery with me,
And my eye gazes on their obstinacy and provocation.
AMP.3:
"Give me a pledge (guarantee, promise) with Yourself [acknowledge my innocence before my death];
Who is there that will be my guarantor and give security for me?
AMP.4:
"But You [Lord] have closed their hearts to understanding,
Therefore You will not exalt them [by giving a verdict against me].
AMP.5:
"He who denounces and informs against his friends for a share of the spoil,
The eyes of his children will also languish and fail.
AMP.6:
"But He has made me a byword and mockery among the people,
And I have become one in whose face people spit.
AMP.7:
"My eye has grown dim (unexpressive) because of grief,
And all my [body's] members are [wasted away] like a shadow.
AMP.8:
"The upright will be [astonished and] appalled at this,
And the innocent will stir himself up against the godless and polluted.
AMP.9:
"Nevertheless the righteous will hold to his ways,
And he who has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.
AMP.10:
"But as for all of you, come back again,
Even though I do not find a wise man among you.
AMP.11:
"My days are past, my purposes and plans are frustrated and torn apart;
The wishes of my heart [are broken].
AMP.12:
"These [thoughts try to] make the night into the day;
'The light is near,' they say in the presence of darkness [but they pervert the truth].
AMP.13:
"But if I look to Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead) as my home,
If I make my bed in the darkness,
AMP.14:
If I call out to the pit (grave), 'You are my father';
And to the worm [that feeds on decay], 'You are my mother and my sister [because I will soon be closest to you],'
AMP.15:
Where now is my hope?
And who regards or considers or is even concerned about my hope?
AMP.16:
"Will my hope go down with me to Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead)?
Shall we go down together in the dust?"

MSG.1:
"My spirit is broken,
my days used up,
my grave dug and waiting.
MSG.2:
See how these mockers close in on me?
How long do I have to put up with their insolence?
MSG.3:
"O God, pledge your support for me.
Give it to me in writing, with your signature.
You're the only one who can do it!
MSG.4:
These people are so useless!
You know firsthand how stupid they can be.
You wouldn't let them have the last word, would you?
MSG.5:
Those who betray their own friends
leave a legacy of abuse to their children.
MSG.6:
"God, you've made me the talk of the town—
people spit in my face;
MSG.7:
I can hardly see from crying so much;
I'm nothing but skin and bones.
MSG.8:
Decent people can't believe what they're seeing;
the good-hearted wake up and insist I've given up on God.
MSG.9:
"But principled people hold tight, keep a firm grip on life,
sure that their clean, pure hands will get stronger and stronger!
MSG.10:
"Maybe you'd all like to start over,
to try it again, the bunch of you.
So far I haven't come across one scrap
of wisdom in anything you've said.
MSG.11:
My life's about over. All my plans are smashed,
all my hopes are snuffed out—
MSG.12:
My hope that night would turn into day,
my hope that dawn was about to break.
MSG.13:
If all I have to look forward to is a home in the graveyard,
if my only hope for comfort is a well-built coffin,
MSG.14:
If a family reunion means going six feet under,
and the only family that shows up is worms,
MSG.15:
Do you call that hope?
Who on earth could find any hope in that?
MSG.16:
No. If hope and I are to be buried together,
I suppose you'll all come to the double funeral!"

NET.1: My spirit is broken, my days have faded out, the grave awaits me.
NET.2: Surely mockery is with me; my eyes must dwell on their hostility.
NET.3: Make then my pledge with you. Who else will put up security for me?
NET.4: Because you have closed their minds to understanding, therefore you will not exalt them.
NET.5: If a man denounces his friends for personal gain, the eyes of his children will fail.
NET.6: He has made me a byword to people, I am the one in whose face they spit.
NET.7: My eyes have grown dim with grief; my whole frame is but a shadow.
NET.8: Upright men are appalled at this; the innocent man is troubled with the godless.
NET.9: But the righteous man holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.
NET.10: “But turn, all of you, and come now! I will not find a wise man among you.
NET.11: My days have passed, my plans are shattered, even the desires of my heart.
NET.12: These men change night into day; they say, ‘The light is near in the face of darkness.’
NET.13: If I hope for the grave to be my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
NET.14: If I cry to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My Mother,’ or ‘My sister,’
NET.15: where then is my hope? And my hope, who sees it?
NET.16: Will it go down to the barred gates of death? Will we descend together into the dust?”
